items.title: 68113_Barney Bigard oral history interview
items.q: I saw that in operation with Rufus Jones in later years when he finally got to quit.

ctx.x: That's true, but he made it so miserable. If he wanted somebody to leave, he made them so miserable that if they had any kind of pride within themselves, that they would just quit, and that would satisfy his ego and it kept his record clear that he's never fired anybody.
I saw that in operation with Rufus Jones in later years when he finally got to quit. Whom did he use it on earlier?

Oh, well, he couldn't do it -- he wanted to do it on Bubber Miley so much but he couldn't because Bubber Miley was the stylist for the band at that time. And he wanted to do it on Otto Hardwick but Otto Hardwick was one of the originals of the Ellington band. So that's about all.
